Direction: profile to tier 2; preserved meaning: the tier-2 law applies
unchanged to the bound objects; narrowed scope: boundaries this profile
governs; invalidation: a change of this profile's definition of any bound
object re-evaluates the binding (P1, P6).

concepts.label: Profile binding to ASSURANCE

concepts.definition: Performed evaluations return a FOUNDATIONS §4 core result directly or through two locally mapped refinements: reconstruction decisions and cross-view axiom verdicts. Ontology and design verdicts are owner dispositions under ACTIVATION §3. Other closed vocabularies are design-record entries, not results: function derivation, entity-lifecycle cells, discovery/admission-form exclusions, competing paths, IACS revision classes, reference mappings, algorithmic obligation dispositions and module roles. Evaluating a record yields a separate core result. An exclusion entry not_applicable leaves the excluded obligation without a result; a not_applicable axiom verdict is instead a value of a declared predicate disjunction including non-application.

grounding.quote:
Purpose and material
relation: a consumer that combines this profile's outcomes with other
results reads each result in the one core and never reads a record entry
as a result (P5, P6).

concepts.label: Results, dispositions and design-record entries

concepts.definition: Realisation-design discipline aims to reduce ambiguity, entropy, avoidable technical debt, hidden authority, hidden mutation and semantic drift; increase refactorability; and preserve auditable reconstruction evidence. Its bias is low coupling, modular composition, immutable typed carriers, total or nearly total transforms and explicit effect boundaries. It applies across module boundaries, schema/carrier families, entity/record design and interface contracts, without a language or runtime monopoly. A module is one possible finite, inspectable intermediate traversal unit, not the only one.

grounding.quote:
The goals are to reduce ambiguity, reduce
entropy, eliminate avoidable technical debt, increase refactorability,
reduce hidden authority, hidden mutation and semantic drift in realisation
code, and preserve enough evidence that later reviewers can audit,
refactor and reconstruct why the realisation took its current shape (P2,
P6). The profile is therefore about realisation design and implementation
shape.

concepts.label: Realisation design purpose and bounded units

conditions: Within a boundary governed by the profile.
concepts.definition: Preferred functionally biased shape: meaning should reside in explicit typed carriers and transforms; imperative coordination should remain subordinate to admitted truth; side effects should be isolated at explicit boundary modules; shared mutable state should be minimised and justified. Functional design discipline is required; a functional programming language is not.

grounding.quote:
The
profile does not require a functional programming language; it does
require a functional design discipline. A Python, Scala, TypeScript,
Kotlin or Java implementation may each satisfy it if it keeps semantic law
in explicit carriers and transforms rather than hidden orchestration.

concepts.label: Functional design discipline

conditions: Within boundaries this profile governs.
concepts.definition: Core realisation rule owned once by SPEC_METHOD §2 Realisation shape and refined by the profile's subsequent rules. Its stated diagnostic is that a design is too imperative and coupled when learning its meaning requires inspecting orchestration.

The core rule, with the test that a design is too imperative and too
coupled when a reader has to inspect orchestration to learn what the
system means, is stated once in

concepts.definition: A deterministic module is a realisation cut inside the graph program. Review first identifies whether the boundary is an operative graph traversal. Typed asset-state movement follows outcome traversal, then declarative graph carriers (GTL and ABG), then deterministic module realisation.

grounding.quote:
If the boundary represents product
movement from one typed asset state to another, the governing shape is:

1. outcome traversal under the graph-execution profile;
2. the declarative graph carrier structure (GTL and ABG in that profile's
   terms); and
3. deterministic module realisation under this profile.

concepts.label: Graph traversal and deterministic realisation alignment

conditions: The profile governs the changed boundary.
concepts.definition: Three overriding boundary-closure evaluators: authority seam closure, essential carrier consolidation and enforcement after proof. Each design or implementation change should be judged against them; they are not optional heuristics. Better ergonomics, tests or static-checker output with failure of an evaluator is not real progress under the profile.

grounding.quote:
When this profile governs a boundary, each design or implementation change
should be judged against three overriding evaluators (P6, P2;
rc.2 #3b-boundary-closure-evaluators). They are not optional heuristics. A
change that improves local ergonomics, test output or static-checker
output but fails one of them is not real progress under this profile.

concepts.label: Overriding boundary-closure evaluators

concepts.definition: Closure of a semantic authority seam requires one authoritative carrier or contract, with no surviving silent reconstruction path when that carrier is removed. Query and projection closure additionally includes coherence with named admitted source truth.

grounding.quote:
The test: if the authoritative carrier
were removed, would the system fail closed, or would another path silently
reconstruct the same meaning? If meaning survives by reconstruction, the
seam is not closed.

concepts.label: Authority seam closure

concepts.definition: Consolidation toward the few real identity-bearing carrier families, beginning with declared IACS and default subordination of Subordinate Payloads. Its progress measure is sharper/fewer families, less duplicate authority and less boundary inflation, rather than additional wrappers, branch-local peer types or public records mirroring payload details.

grounding.quote:
Each change should collapse the slice to the few real identity-bearing
carrier families (P3, P2; rc.2 #2-essential-carrier-consolidation). This
means declaring the IACS first (§6), keeping Subordinate Payloads
subordinate by default, and avoiding fragment classes, interfaces or result
records created only to satisfy typing, serialisation or convenience
extraction. Progress is fewer, sharper carrier families, less duplicate
authority and less boundary inflation; not one more wrapper layer, one more
branch-local peer type, or one more public record that only mirrors
payload detail.

concepts.label: Essential carrier consolidation

concepts.definition: Language-independent sequence: parse, validate or construct; explicitly admit and narrow; then enforce the already-proved shape with typing, schemas, validators, contracts or codecs. Examples include mypy --strict, sealed algebraic type plus parser, or compiler-enforced sum type plus decoder.

grounding.quote:
Typing, schemas, validators, contracts and codecs exist to lock in a seam
that has already been made real (P6, P1; rc.2 #3-enforcement-after-proof).
Parse, validate or construct first; admit and narrow the boundary
explicitly; then use types or schemas to enforce the proved shape.

concepts.label: Proof before enforcement

concepts.definition: Ingress conversion receives foreign input, parses/validates/normalises once, constructs admitted local carrier truth, and exposes only that local truth to semantic kernels.
concepts.label: Ingress collapse

conditions: The profile governs repo-authored Python at the adopted boundary.
concepts.definition: Python semantic design uses fully annotated callable parameters/returns and closed typed carriers, including tests, scripts and support code at the production bar. Closed forms may include dataclass, TypedDict, Protocol, Literal, Enum or equivalents. Strict static checking, such as mypy --strict or an equivalent strict configuration, is required.

grounding.quote:
When this profile governs a Python boundary, repo-authored Python is fully
typed (P1; rc.2 #4a-python-typing-rule): every function, method and
callable surface has explicit parameter and return annotations; semantic
carriers are closed and typed; and repo-authored tests, scripts and
support code are typed too, with no lower bar than production code.

concepts.label: Governed Python boundary

concepts.definition: Engineering Ontology of one designed boundary consists of entities, identities, relationships, invariants, lifecycle, authority, atomic functions, higher-order composition, effects and projections. Once accepted it is the prior semantic-design authority, subordinate to constitutional intent, Product, requirements and applicable graph/domain profiles. Accepted target design remains the structural HOW: topology, interfaces, carrier placement, module boundaries, algorithms and local realisation. A class, schema, endpoint, command or carrier inventory alone is not an Ontology.

grounding.quote:
Ontology =
  entities + identities + relationships + invariants + lifecycle
  + authority + atomic functions + higher-order composition
  + effects + projections

concepts.label: Ontology and accepted semantic basis

U(B) = unresolved(M(B))
decision_complete(B) iff
  U(B) = empty
  and M(B) is jointly satisfiable
  and every network admitted by M(B) is semantically equivalent under the
      governing Product, requirements and accepted design relations
co_evolution_admissible(B) iff decision_complete(B)
design_gate(B) =
  the smallest causally closed affected set needed to establish
  decision_complete(B)

  + authorities + authority transitions + functions
  + higher-order composition laws + topology
  + lifecycle states and transitions + public contracts
  + externally observable Product meaning

concepts.label: Complete material-relation network M(B)

concepts.definition: A material design frame declares its governing accepted frames/relations, proposed action's bounded affected relation set, inherited invariants, crossing authority/composition seams, and subordinate frames opened by unresolved material distinctions. Global and local are relative to the selected frame. Governing frames form a constraint network, possibly with several parents rather than a compulsory hierarchy.
concepts.label: Bounded design frame

concepts.definition: Native constructability is the selected substrate's ability to construct the design's required identities, relationships, transitions, authority boundaries, effects, lifecycle, composition, publication and retirement behaviour. It is an acceptance obligation, not a prescribed implementation.

grounding.quote:
A semantically coherent design is not acceptable when its selected
substrate cannot natively construct the required identities,
relationships, transitions, authority boundaries, effects, lifecycle,
composition, publication and retirement behaviour (P2, P5;
rc.2 #native-constructability-before-design-acceptance-stdo-up-002). A missing
substrate capability remains an explicit design gap or triggers lawful
re-entry (SPEC_METHOD §4); it is not hidden behind a reference bridge,
adapter, filesystem runner, test double or promised future feature (P6;
SPEC_METHOD §7 Bridge prohibition). This is a constructability obligation,
not a prescribed implementation; the consumer chooses the substrate and the
evidence mechanism (P0).

concepts.label: Native constructability

conditions: Before constructing a material generic capability, common mechanic or algorithm, or selecting a material dependency.
concepts.definition: Proportional bounded foundation-selection procedure refining FOUNDATIONS §4 Shared machinery. It compares candidate compositions drawn from admitted project foundations; language/runtime/platform/standard-library capabilities; accepted predecessor or immutable-lineage realisations usable as evidence; maintained external foundations where dependencies are permitted; and bounded local implementation. Constructability alone does not establish local construction as best.
exceptions: No package survey or ledger is required for a trivial helper whose choice cannot materially affect authority, Product behaviour, lifecycle cost or the accepted design network.

grounding.quote:
The bounded candidate population draws applicable compositions from:
foundations already admitted in the current project; language, runtime,
platform or standard-library capabilities; accepted predecessor or
immutable-lineage realisations usable as evidence; maintained external
foundations where the Product permits a dependency; and a bounded local
implementation (P2).

concepts.label: Capability and foundation selection

conditions: Among lawful candidate compositions on the current declared basis.
concepts.definition: Dominance holds only if every material decision dimension is comparable or evidenced non-discriminating, one composition is no worse on every comparable dimension and strictly better on at least one. Material unknowns that could reverse this prevent dominance. Materially incomparable lawful candidates form an explicit undominated frontier.

grounding.quote:
One lawful candidate composition dominates another on the current basis
only when every material decision dimension is comparable or evidenced as
non-discriminating between them, it is no worse on every comparable
dimension, and it is strictly better on at least one. A material unknown
that could reverse the relation prevents dominance and remains a gap. A
dominated candidate cannot be selected unless new evidence or another
material dimension invalidates the dominance relation; therefore a local
rebuild of generic mechanics is inadmissible when an existing lawful
foundation composition dominates it. Unused feature breadth alone does not
establish dominance and may itself add lifecycle cost (P2, P6).

concepts.label: Evidence-bounded dominance and frontier

conditions: For identity-bearing entities and independently governed value families inside the active boundary.
concepts.definition: Logical-completeness matrix or equivalent closed representation identifies Entity, Identity, Authority owner, Declare/create, Read/project, Update/transition and Delete/retire, alongside Ontology relationships, cardinalities, invariants and lifecycle states. These are completeness questions rather than a mutable-CRUD mandate. Entity lifecycle describes domain states/transformations, distinct from ASSURANCE §16's build/release/deploy/observe/retire operational module lifecycle.
exceptions: Subordinate Payloads and value objects inherit their owner's lifecycle and authority without a ceremonial peer row unless they pass the Promotion Test.

grounding.quote:

rewrite it. A result that changes a governing relation re-enters at that
relation before acceptance (P4b; FOUNDATIONS §3 P4b, frame instance). A
subordinate frame opens only when a material distinction cannot be
resolved at the governing altitude; this rule does not require recursively
documenting irrelevant descendants (P2). The law is false if a change is
locally valid inside the selected frame but violates, duplicates or
silently reinterprets an invariant in any affected governing frame.

constraints.statement: Evaluate against every affected governing frame, preserve every applicable accepted relation, update only affected subordinate projections, and re-enter changed governing relations before acceptance. Declared seams make the affected set testable without a closure algorithm or irrelevant expansion. Discovered verbs/screens/endpoints/commands/ticket phrases/use cases are behavioural evidence, not immediately public operation identities, peer carriers, modules or functions. Derivation order is constitutional functionality → candidate Ontology → logical completeness → whole-family Prime contraction → accepted Ontology basis → IACS → target design and domain/sequence/state projections → public-contract/adapter projections → implementation/test projections.

grounding.quote:
Candidate discovery is bounded, reproducible and explicitly
non-exhaustive. For every candidate category the evidence record declares
the sources or collections searched, cutoff time and relevant version
basis, applicability and inclusion criteria, material exclusions,
predecessor or incumbent status, discovered candidates and residual
unknowns; a category not searched records `not_applicable` or a named gap
with its reason. Discovery closes only for that declared basis and cutoff.
A discovery gap that could materially alter the frontier prevents
selection; an immaterial residual records why it cannot change the current
decision. A later candidate that satisfies the applicability criteria and
could materially alter the lawful frontier invalidates the affected
selection evidence and re-enters this relation (P6, P5, P3); such a
candidate is newly acquired admissible evidence material to the selection,
an instance of the material input change of
[ACTIVATION §7](ACTIVATION.md#7-closed-result-and-reuse).

Every category records searched sources/collections, cutoff/version, applicability/inclusion criteria, material exclusions, predecessor/incumbent status, candidates and unknowns; an unsearched category records reasoned not_applicable or named gap. Closure is only for that basis/cutoff. A potentially frontier-changing discovery gap prevents selection; an immaterial residual explains why it cannot alter the decision. Hard authority, Product-contract, safety, security, licensing or constructability failure eliminates. Unknowns stay unknown, not favourable scores; no universal scalar is required. Dominated candidates cannot be selected while dominance holds, including local rebuild dominated by lawful foundation composition; unused features alone do not establish dominance and may cost lifecycle effort. The existing trade-off owner selects only a lawful undominated composition by exact-Product/basis declared priorities and risk tolerances, recording frontier resolution. If unresolved, keep a design gap. Rejected material candidates record decisive evidence/falsifier. Unsupported preference is not closure; fewest dependencies, smallest edit, least local code or richest features are not necessarily the answer.

preserves the declared relation's owner, role kind, subject, scope, basis

written code; an irreducible Product or domain relation retains its
declared owner whether local code, a reused foundation or their
composition realises it. Generic local code is lawful only when it wins
the same comparison; it is not the default (P6).
